votes.reason: LMT trades at 21.5x trailing earnings with EPS up 52.8% on the four quarters before, so it is still a sound defense prime at a fair price even after its 14.36% 12-week run.

At 43.6x trailing earnings with EPS down 0.9%, CAT is by far the most expensive name in the book (the next is JNJ at 24.3x): a cyclical machinery maker priced like a growth stock while its earnings shrink, which leaves no margin of safety.

At 24.3x trailing with EPS still growing 8.6%, JNJ is fairly priced rather than cheap after its 16.6% 12-week run, but it is a sound business at a reasonable multiple for its quality, so my lens gives no concrete reason against it.
At 11.3x trailing with EPS up 10.1%, PGR is the cheapest name in the book and a high-quality insurer, exactly the cheap and sound profile I look for.

COP's 20.2x trailing multiple comes from earnings that fell with the cycle (EPS down 24.1%), not from a stretched price, since the stock is down 1.65% over 12 weeks, so a sound large producer held at 10% as a hedge gives my lens no concrete reason to object.
